ja: だいにじゅうごしょう

p.src: (with a bunch of keys and a lamp, before an iron door)

u.src: (with a bunch of keys and a lamp, before an iron door)

p.src: A shudder, long unfelt, comes o’er me; Mankind’s collected woe o’erwhelms me, here. She dwells within the dark, damp walls before me, And all her crime was a delusion dear! What! I delay to free her? I dread, once again to see her? On! my shrinking but lingers Death more near.

u.src: A shudder, long unfelt, comes o’er me; Mankind’s collected woe o’erwhelms me, here.
She dwells within the dark, damp walls before me, And all her crime was a delusion dear!
I dread, once again to see her?
On! my shrinking but lingers Death more near.

p.src: (He grasps the lock: the sound of singing is heard inside.)

u.src: (He grasps the lock: the sound of singing is heard inside.)

p.src: My mother, the harlot, Who put me to death; My father, the varlet, Who eaten me hath! Little sister, so good, Laid my bones in the wood, In the damp moss and clay: Then was I a beautiful bird o’ the wood; Fly away! Fly away!

u.src: My mother, the harlot, Who put me to death; My father, the varlet, Who eaten me hath!
Little sister, so good, Laid my bones in the wood, In the damp moss and clay: Then was I a beautiful bird o’ the wood; Fly away!

p.src: She does not dream her lover listens near; That he the rattling chain, the rustling straw, can hear.

u.src: She does not dream her lover listens near; That he the rattling chain, the rustling straw, can hear.

p.src: MARGARET (hiding herself on the pallet) Woe! woe! They come. O death of bitterness!

u.src: MARGARET (hiding herself on the pallet) Woe! woe!

p.src: FAUST (whispering) Hush! hush! The hour is come that frees thee.

u.src: The hour is come that frees thee.

p.src: MARGARET (throwing herself before him) Art thou a man, then pity my distress!

u.src: MARGARET (throwing herself before him) Art thou a man, then pity my distress!

p.src: FAUST Thy cries will wake the guards, and they will seize thee! (He takes hold of the fetters to unlock them.)

u.src: FAUST Thy cries will wake the guards, and they will seize thee!
(He takes hold of the fetters to unlock them.)

p.src: Who, headsman! unto thee such power Over me could give? Thou’rt come for me at midnight-hour: Have mercy on me, let me live! Is’t not soon enough when morning chime has run?

u.src: Who, headsman! unto thee such power Over me could give?
Thou’rt come for me at midnight-hour: Have mercy on me, let me live!
Is’t not soon enough when morning chime has run?

p.src: And I am yet so young, so young! And now Death comes, and ruin! I, too, was fair, and that was my undoing. My love was near, but now he’s far; Torn lies the wreath, scattered the blossoms are. Seize me not thus so violently! Spare me! What have I done to thee? Let me not vainly entreat thee! I never chanced, in all my days, to meet thee!

u.src: And I am yet so young, so young!
And now Death comes, and ruin!
I, too, was fair, and that was my undoing.
My love was near, but now he’s far; Torn lies the wreath, scattered the blossoms are.
Seize me not thus so violently!
What have I done to thee?
Let me not vainly entreat thee!
I never chanced, in all my days, to meet thee!

p.src: Now am I wholly in thy might. But let me suckle, first, my baby! I nursed it all this livelong night; They took ’t away, to vex me, maybe, And now they say I killed the child outright. And never shall I be glad again. They sing songs about me! ’tis bad of the folk to do it! There’s an old story has the same refrain; Who bade them so construe it?

u.src: Now am I wholly in thy might.
But let me suckle, first, my baby!
I nursed it all this livelong night; They took ’t away, to vex me, maybe, And now they say I killed the child outright.
And never shall I be glad again.
’tis bad of the folk to do it!
There’s an old story has the same refrain; Who bade them so construe it?

p.src: Here lieth one who loves thee ever, The thraldom of thy woe to sever.

u.src: Here lieth one who loves thee ever, The thraldom of thy woe to sever.

p.src: O let us kneel, and call the Saints to hide us! Under the steps beside us, The threshold under, Hell heaves in thunder! The Evil One With terrible wrath Seeketh a path His prey to discover!

u.src: O let us kneel, and call the Saints to hide us!
Under the steps beside us, The threshold under, Hell heaves in thunder!
The Evil One With terrible wrath Seeketh a path His prey to discover!

p.src: That was the voice of my lover!

u.src: That was the voice of my lover!

p.src: (She springs to her feet: the fetters fall off.)

u.src: (She springs to her feet: the fetters fall off.)

p.src: Where is he? I heard him call me. I am free! No one shall enthrall me. To his neck will I fly, On his bosom lie! On the threshold he stood, and Margaret! calling, Midst of Hell’s howling and noises appalling, Midst of the wrathful, infernal derision, I knew the sweet sound of the voice of the vision!

u.src: To his neck will I fly, On his bosom lie!
On the threshold he stood, and Margaret! calling, Midst of Hell’s howling and noises appalling, Midst of the wrathful, infernal derision, I knew the sweet sound of the voice of the vision!

p.src: ’Tis thou! O, say it once again!

’Tis he! ’tis he! Where now is all my pain? The anguish of the dungeon, and the chain? ’Tis thou! Thou comest to save me, And I am saved!— Again the street I see Where first I looked on thee; And the garden, brightly blooming, Where I and Martha wait thy coming.

u.src: Where now is all my pain?
The anguish of the dungeon, and the chain?
Thou comest to save me, And I am saved!— Again the street I see Where first I looked on thee; And the garden, brightly blooming, Where I and Martha wait thy coming.

p.src: Delay, now! So fain I stay, when thou delayest!

u.src: So fain I stay, when thou delayest!

p.src: Away, now! If longer here thou stayest, We shall be made to dearly rue it.

u.src: If longer here thou stayest, We shall be made to dearly rue it.

p.src: Kiss me!—canst no longer do it? My friend, so short a time thou’rt missing, And hast unlearned thy kissing? Why is my heart so anxious, on thy breast? Where once a heaven thy glances did create me, A heaven thy loving words expressed, And thou didst kiss, as thou wouldst suffocate me— Kiss me! Or I’ll kiss thee!

u.src: Kiss me!—canst no longer do it?
My friend, so short a time thou’rt missing, And hast unlearned thy kissing?
Why is my heart so anxious, on thy breast?
Where once a heaven thy glances did create me, A heaven thy loving words expressed, And thou didst kiss, as thou wouldst suffocate me— Kiss me!

p.src: Ah, woe! thy lips are chill, And still. How changed in fashion Thy passion! Who has done me this ill?

u.src: Ah, woe! thy lips are chill, And still.
How changed in fashion Thy passion!
Who has done me this ill?

p.src: Come, follow me! My darling, be more bold: I’ll clasp thee, soon, with warmth a thousand-fold; But follow now! ’Tis all I beg of thee.

u.src: My darling, be more bold: I’ll clasp thee, soon, with warmth a thousand-fold; But follow now!

p.src: And is it thou? Thou, surely, certainly?
And in thy lap wilt take me once again. How comes it that thou dost not shrink from me?— Say, dost thou know, my friend, whom thou mak’st free?

u.src: And in thy lap wilt take me once again.
How comes it that thou dost not shrink from me?— Say, dost thou know, my friend, whom thou mak’st free?

p.src: Come! come! The night already vanisheth.

My mother have I put to death; I’ve drowned the baby born to thee. Was it not given to thee and me? Thee, too!—’Tis thou! It scarcely true doth seem— Give me thy hand! ’Tis not a dream! Thy dear, dear hand!—But, ah, ’tis wet! Why, wipe it off! Methinks that yet There’s blood thereon. Ah, God! what hast thou done? Nay, sheathe thy sword at last! Do not affray me!

u.src: My mother have I put to death; I’ve drowned the baby born to thee.
Was it not given to thee and me?
It scarcely true doth seem— Give me thy hand!
Thy dear, dear hand!—But, ah, ’tis wet!
Methinks that yet There’s blood thereon.
Ah, God! what hast thou done?
Nay, sheathe thy sword at last!

p.src: O, let the past be past! Thy words will slay me!

u.src: O, let the past be past!

p.src: No, no! Thou must outlive us. Now I’ll tell thee the graves to give us: Thou must begin to-morrow The work of sorrow! The best place give to my mother, Then close at her side my brother, And me a little away, But not too very far, I pray! And here, on my right breast, my baby lay! Nobody else will lie beside me!— Ah, within thine arms to hide me, That was a sweet and a gracious bliss, But no more, no more can I attain it! I would force myself on thee and constrain it, And it seems thou repellest my kiss: And yet ’tis thou, so good, so kind to see!

u.src: Now I’ll tell thee the graves to give us: Thou must begin to-morrow The work of sorrow!
The best place give to my mother, Then close at her side my brother, And me a little away, But not too very far, I pray!
And here, on my right breast, my baby lay!
Nobody else will lie beside me!— Ah, within thine arms to hide me, That was a sweet and a gracious bliss, But no more, no more can I attain it!
I would force myself on thee and constrain it, And it seems thou repellest my kiss: And yet ’tis thou, so good, so kind to see!

p.src: If thou feel’st it is I, then come with me!

u.src: If thou feel’st it is I, then come with me!

p.src: If the grave is there, Death lying in wait, then come! From here to eternal rest: No further step—no, no! Thou goest away! O Henry, if I could go!

u.src: If the grave is there, Death lying in wait, then come!
From here to eternal rest: No further step—no, no!
O Henry, if I could go!

p.src: Thou canst! Just will it! Open stands the door.

I dare not go: there’s no hope any more. Why should I fly? They’ll still my steps waylay! It is so wretched, forced to beg my living, And a bad conscience sharper misery giving! It is so wretched, to be strange, forsaken, And I’d still be followed and taken!

u.src: I dare not go: there’s no hope any more.
It is so wretched, forced to beg my living, And a bad conscience sharper misery giving!
It is so wretched, to be strange, forsaken, And I’d still be followed and taken!

p.src: Be quick! Be quick! Save thy perishing child! Away! Follow the ridge Up by the brook,

u.src: Follow the ridge Up by the brook,

p.src: If the grave is there, Death lying in wait, then come!

u.src: If the grave is there, Death lying in wait, then come!

p.src: Over the bridge, Into the wood, To the left, where the plank is placed In the pool! Seize it in haste! ’Tis trying to rise, ’Tis struggling still! Save it! Save it!

u.src: Over the bridge, Into the wood, To the left, where the plank is placed In the pool!

p.src: Recall thy wandering will! One step, and thou art free at last!

u.src: One step, and thou art free at last!

p.src: If the mountain we had only passed! There sits my mother upon a stone,— I feel an icy shiver! There sits my mother upon a stone, And her head is wagging ever. She beckons, she nods not, her heavy head falls o’er; She slept so long that she wakes no more. She slept, while we were caressing: Ah, those were the days of blessing!

u.src: If the mountain we had only passed!
There sits my mother upon a stone,— I feel an icy shiver!
There sits my mother upon a stone, And her head is wagging ever.
She beckons, she nods not, her heavy head falls o’er; She slept so long that she wakes no more.
She slept, while we were caressing: Ah, those were the days of blessing!

p.src: Here words and prayers are nothing worth; I’ll venture, then, to bear thee forth.

u.src: Here words and prayers are nothing worth; I’ll venture, then, to bear thee forth.

p.src: No—let me go! I’ll suffer no force! Grasp me not so murderously! I’ve done, else, all things for the love of thee.

u.src: I’ve done, else, all things for the love of thee.

p.src: Day? Yes, the day comes,—the last day breaks for me! My wedding-day it was to be! Tell no one thou hast been with Margaret! Woe for my garland! The chances Are over—’tis all in vain! We shall meet once again, But not at the dances! The crowd is thronging, no word is spoken: The square below And the streets overflow: The death-bell tolls, the wand is broken. I am seized, and bound, and delivered— Shoved to the block—they give the sign! Now over each neck has quivered The blade that is quivering over mine. Dumb lies the world like the grave!

u.src: Yes, the day comes,—the last day breaks for me!
My wedding-day it was to be!
Tell no one thou hast been with Margaret!
The chances Are over—’tis all in vain!
We shall meet once again, But not at the dances!
The crowd is thronging, no word is spoken: The square below And the streets overflow: The death-bell tolls, the wand is broken.
I am seized, and bound, and delivered— Shoved to the block—they give the sign!
Now over each neck has quivered The blade that is quivering over mine.
Dumb lies the world like the grave!

p.src: O had I ne’er been born!

u.src: O had I ne’er been born!

p.src: Off! or you’re lost ere morn. Useless talking, delaying and praying! My horses are neighing: The morning twilight is near.

u.src: Off! or you’re lost ere morn.
My horses are neighing: The morning twilight is near.

p.src: What rises up from the threshold here? He! he! suffer him not! What does he want in this holy spot? He seeks me!

u.src: What rises up from the threshold here?
What does he want in this holy spot?

p.src: Judgment of God! myself to thee I give.

u.src: Judgment of God! myself to thee I give.

p.src: Come! or I’ll leave her in the lurch, and thee!

u.src: Come! or I’ll leave her in the lurch, and thee!

p.src: Thine am I, Father! rescue me! Ye angels, holy cohorts, guard me, Camp around, and from evil ward me! Henry! I shudder to think of thee.

u.src: Thine am I, Father! rescue me!
Ye angels, holy cohorts, guard me, Camp around, and from evil ward me!
I shudder to think of thee.
